# Trellis's SwiftTerm source snapshot

Upstream: SwiftTerm 1.20.0, revision `5d14406844143538cd8f8851d2d8a67c1fe443e5`, from https://github.com/migueldeicaza/SwiftTerm. MIT license: [LICENSE](LICENSE).

This directory contains the upstream `Sources/SwiftTerm` tree and a minimal macOS library package. The shader resource retains its `SwiftTerm_SwiftTerm.bundle` identity. Demo applications, command-line tools, documentation plugins, and unrelated dependencies are omitted. `SwiftTermBuildInfo.swift` records the pinned upstream identity with the modified-build flag, replacing the upstream build-info generator.

The exact engine delta is [trellis.patch](trellis.patch). It changes nine upstream files:

- `Mac/MacTerminalView.swift`: makes mouse-exit and scroll-wheel overrides open so the Trellis wrapper can reveal its scrollbar on track hover or actual viewport scrolling and fade it when idle. Engine scrolling behavior is unchanged. A `doubleClickSelection` hook lets the host replace double-click word selection with smart selection (FR-C06); it is consulted only after mouse reporting declines the click and falls back to `selectWordOrExpression` when it returns nil. `bufferPosition(for:)` exposes the BiDi-aware mouse hit test for context-menu link actions (FR-L05). Text-rendering properties (FR-TX01, FR-TX03): `fontLigatures` rebuilds the font set with the `calt`, `liga` and `dlig` OpenType features off, because programming fonts join characters through contextual alternates that `kCTLigatureAttributeName` doesn't control. The `font` getter returns the host's font (`FontSet.base`), so toggling ligatures isn't seen as a font change. `allowBoldFont` and `allowItalicFont` choose the regular face for bold or italic text, `boldIsBright` controls bold-as-bright for ANSI colors 0-7, and `textBlinkEnabled` stops text blinking. Each redraws only when its value changes and none resizes the grid.
- `Apple/AppleTerminalView.swift`: a font change resizes without DECSTR. Upstream's view-level resize soft-resets application cursor mode, attributes, and other live parser state. OSC 8 parameters are split from the URL at the first `;` only, as `Terminal.parseHyperlinkPayload` already does, so a URL containing `;` is not truncated. Text rendering (FR-TX01, FR-TX02, FR-TX03):
  - Runs are placed on the grid from their source cells (`CTRunGetStringRange`/`CTRunGetStringIndices`, via the public `TerminalGlyphPlacement`) rather than from glyph counts. Upstream positioned glyph *i* at column *i* and sized backgrounds by glyph count, so a font ligature that merges characters shifted the rest of the row. The identity fast path remains for runs with one glyph per one-unit cell.
  - Underline, strikethrough and the new overline are stroked once across the run's columns, not one cell per glyph, so they cover wide characters and ligatures. Dash, dot and curl patterns are phased from the row origin.
  - Concealed text (SGR 8) is drawn like blinking text in its hidden phase: background kept, glyphs and decorations removed. Upstream stored the flag but drew the text.
  - While ligatures are on, the cell under a visible cursor is shaped as its own segment, and a cursor move invalidates the rows it left and entered. A new segment also starts at each change of face, because CoreText shapes contextual alternates across font runs (a regular `-` before a bold `>` became half an arrow).
  - Font selection goes through `styledFont(bold:italic:)` for cells and the caret. `mapColor` brightens bold ANSI colors 0-7 when `boldIsBright` is on; upstream's `< 7` check skipped white (7).
  - `renderedRowForTesting(_:)` exposes the runs the CoreGraphics path draws, built by the same code. The Metal renderer is unchanged and doesn't honor these settings; Trellis doesn't enable it.
- `SelectionService.swift`: `setWordSelection(start:end:)` sets a half-open, word-mode selection with its drag anchor. `setSelection` clamps the end to `cols - 1` and leaves character mode, which would drop a token's last column and extend drags by character.
- `Buffer.swift`: an opt-in `reflowCursorLine` flag permits normal-buffer current-line reflow. It captures the logical cursor cell offset before resize clamps the cursor, maps it to a destination row object, and restores its position after reflow and history trimming. Destination identity handles eviction of earlier rows in the same logical group; wide-character wrap padding and pending-wrap boundaries are accounted for. The wider reflow loop reads the current wrapped group's first row, rather than row zero of the entire buffer.
- `KittyGraphics.swift`: Kitty graphics file (`t=f`), temporary-file (`t=t`), and shared-memory (`t=s`) transmission are refused with `ENOTSUP`. Terminal output is untrusted (NFR-S05); it must not make the app read, probe for, or unlink local files or POSIX shared memory. Direct (`t=d`) transmission is unchanged.
- `CharData.swift`: `Attribute.extendedStyle` (`ExtendedCharacterStyle`) carries overline, because all eight `CharacterStyle` bits are taken. It fits in existing padding, so `CharData` stays 24 bytes; it's part of attribute equality and of `toSgr()`, and `justColor()` drops it.
- `Mac/MacCaretView.swift`: the caret hides concealed text like the cells beneath it.
- `iOS/iOSTerminalView.swift`: plain copies of the text-style properties so the shared renderer still compiles for iOS. The vendored package builds only for macOS, so this file isn't compiled here.
- `Terminal.swift`: parses overline (SGR 53, reset by 55 and 0) and treats rapid blink (SGR 6) as blink; upstream logged both as unknown. It also exposes the normal-buffer opt-in. Trellis enables it only during font changes. Ordinary frame resizing and alternate-screen reflow policies remain upstream behavior. It also adds `handleSemanticPrompt(_:)`, a public forwarder to the built-in OSC 133 handler, so Trellis's own 133 handler can authenticate shell-integration marks (FR-SI02) and still keep upstream prompt marks and navigation state. `handleProgressReport(_:)` likewise forwards to the built-in OSC 9;4 progress handling, so Trellis's OSC 9 notification handler (FR-T06) keeps the progress bar. `linkIsExplicit(at:)` says whether a cell holds an OSC 8 hyperlink, because the delegate's `requestOpenLink` can't tell a hyperlink target from detected text and Trellis refuses schemeless hyperlink targets (FR-L04).

The wrapper still preserves native selections independently with logical Unicode offsets. Explicit history eviction clears selections whose text was removed, rather than selecting another identical occurrence. Alternate-screen applications own their screen contents and redraw after a geometry change; cells clipped by their screen-oriented resize are outside the retained-text selection guarantee.

For an update, replace the source tree from a verified upstream revision, reapply or retire each delta, update this provenance/build identity, and run the complete Trellis suite plus native appearance, zoom, clipboard, search, and alternate-screen checks. `TerminalSelectionBookmarkTests` and `TerminalAppearanceTests` cover current/completed row selection, repeated/wide/combining/ZWJ text, cursor continuation after narrow/wide reflow, history reduction, and live session/mode preservation. Regenerate `trellis.patch` against the recorded upstream snapshot after changing the delta: for each changed file, `git diff --no-index` from the upstream file to the vendored one, with `a/` and `b/` paths relative to the upstream root. `git apply trellis.patch` on a clean upstream checkout must reproduce this tree except `SwiftTermBuildInfo.swift`. `SmartSelectionTerminalTests` and `TerminalFileLinkTests` cover the selection hook and link classification. `TerminalTextStyleTests`, `TerminalLigatureTests` and `TerminalUnicodeWidthTests` cover the text-rendering delta.
